headline: Service stopping now ends all open watches via closeWatches
reason: Shutdown path now actively terminates in-flight streaming requests, which changes lifecycle and client-visible behavior.
summary: When the service enters stopping, after marking not-ready it now calls router.closeWatches() to end every open watch so the HTTP server's Shutdown does not block on never-idle connections. Clients see their watch streams end and must re-establish them against another replica.
focus: closeWatches is safe to call concurrently with reconcile/publish and more than once (stopping may run after reconcile already ended entries)
watches opened after closeWatches returns during the shutdown window are also ended or rejected, not left to block Shutdown
closeWatches covers watches served by the single-tenant fallback and in-process backends, not only routed handler entries
ending the stream yields a clean end the client can resume from, not an aborted connection
